identity.description: Notion is an all-in-one workspace (notes, docs, databases, project management). Its public REST API is documented at developers.notion.com, and Notion publishes an official hosted MCP server.
identity.identity_notes: developers.notion.com documents the Notion public API (api.notion.com) for pages, databases, comments, users, and search; the product is the Notion workspace app from notion.com. Confirmed as the Notion productivity app named in the assignment.

auth.oauth_flows: OAuth 2.0 authorization for public and scoped integrations; exact grant types beyond the authorization flow not verified.
auth.scopes_notes: Internal connections use static tokens; OAuth integrations choose installation scope (for example 'any workspace for public integrations'). Detailed capability scopes not verified.

access.production_restrictions: Internal connection creation requires the workspace owner role; Business/Enterprise admins may restrict PAT creation. Public OAuth integrations: source says marketplace submission/review is not required to begin authorization; listing rules not verified.

api.rate_limits: Per connection, a fixed budget per 60-second window: 180 requests/min (about 3/s) on all other plans; 600 requests/min (about 10/s) on Business and Enterprise.
api.limitations: Requires Authorization Bearer token and Notion-Version header. Webhook event list includes page.content_updated (aggregated, may be delayed), comment.created (needs comment read capability), data_source.schema_updated; database.schema_updated is deprecated. Official SDK is JavaScript (makenotion/notion-sdk-js); no other official SDK language was confirmed. Write-op list is partial; only page creation and file uploads were directly verified.

claims.value: Notion public API at developers.notion.com for building tools that create pages, organize data, and share feedback
claims.quote: Build tools and automations that create pages, organize data, and share feedback in Notion.
Send requests over HTTPS to https://api.notion.com. To make your first request, follow the API quickstart.

claims.value: Bearer token (personal access token / internal connection token)
claims.quote: Internal connections use a static credential called an internal connection API token
OAuth integrations follow the OAuth 2.0 protocol to authorize a connection to interact with a workspace.

claims.value: Workspace owner required to create an internal connection
claims.quote: You are required to be a workspace owner to create a connection.

claims.value: Marketplace review not required to begin OAuth authorization
claims.quote: You can start authorization as soon as you configure the integration's client credentials and redirect URI.

claims.value: Business/Enterprise workspaces may restrict PAT creation
claims.quote: Business and Enterprise workspaces may restrict PAT creation, so an owner might need to enable it.

claims.value: Webhooks supported; subscriptions created in connection settings Webhooks tab
claims.quote: Webhooks let your connection receive real-time updates from Notion.
Use the JavaScript SDK, curl, or any client that can send HTTPS requests.

claims.value: 180 req/min (avg 3/s) for most plans; 600 req/min (avg 10/s) for Business and Enterprise
claims.quote: 180 requests per minute (an average of 3 per second)

claims.value: Notion-maintained hosted MCP server at https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
claims.quote: "Notion MCP" (`https://mcp.notion.com/mcp`) is our hosted, actively maintained server.

claims.value: Hosted MCP uses OAuth and MCP tokens
claims.quote: It supports OAuth authorization and MCP tokens, and requires no infrastructure setup.

claims.value: makenotion/notion-mcp-server (MIT, owned by makenotion org) is no longer actively maintained; hosted server is recommended
claims.quote: This repository is a separate, self-hosted MCP server implementation that is no longer actively maintained or supported.

Whether community-maintained third-party MCP servers (not in the makenotion org) exist with verified repos was not confirmed; directory listings such as mcpservers.org and Docker Hub were seen but not verified repositories.
Webhook signature verification and full event catalog were not fully confirmed.
